newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George-less market exuberance in UK than US.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George-less market exuberance in UK than US.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday there may be some of "irrational exuberance" in Britain's financial markets, but if it was there, it was probably less extreme than in the United States.

"The view from the stock market is very important. Of course we are aware of perceptions of 'irrational exuberance' which could have monetary effects," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.
"But if there is irrational exuberance here, it is probably a bit less than in the United States."
Late last year, U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent U.S. stock and bond markets spiralling lower by warning of "irrational exuberance" in the markets.
But giving testimony to Congress over the past two days, Greenspan has painted a much more market-friendly picture of steady but slowing U.S. economic growth and low inflation.
